commands.name: inspect
commands.description: Print what a supplier reads first: the package's identity, its guide, its inputs, outputs, references and examples, and the commands to run next.
commands.detail:
The package is a packed package file or a source directory. Before it prints anything, inspect verifies the whole package: every entry's name and data, the digest of every entry and of the package, the manifest under the specification version it declares, every schema, and each compiled file against the sources it is derived from. A package that fails any check is refused with every finding of the check, and nothing of it is printed.

The digest of a source directory is the digest of the package metais pack would write from it, computed in memory; nothing is written.

A guide of more than 60 lines or 6144 bytes is cut to its first 40 lines, within 4096 bytes; --guide prints it whole, and nothing else.

commands.name: ls
commands.description: List the entries under a path of a package.
commands.detail:
With no path, lists the root. A path that names a directory lists its children, or with --recursive every file and directory beneath it; a path that names a file lists that file. Directories are implied by the entries' paths. The listing is in the byte order of the paths, a directory's written with its trailing /.

A packed package's entries are the zip's, .compiled/ included; a source directory's are the files metais pack would write from it, without .compiled/. Paths use / on every platform and are matched byte for byte, case-sensitively; the root is . or omitted.

commands.name: read
commands.description: Print an entry of a package, or a range of its lines.
commands.detail:
Prints the entry's bytes exactly as stored. An entry is text when it is valid UTF-8 and holds no NUL byte, and binary otherwise. A line ends at an LF; an entry has as many lines as LFs, plus one when it is not empty and does not end with an LF.

--lines takes N (one line), N-M or N- (to the end), 1-based and inclusive, with N at least 1 and M at least N. A range that starts beyond the last line is refused; an end beyond it is read to the last line. The lines are printed with their own line endings. --number prefixes each line with its number and a tab. Both read lines of text, and refuse a binary entry; a binary entry is not written to a terminal.

With --json, a text entry is the string content, with the lines read and the entry's line count; a binary entry is content_base64.

operands.name: <package>
operands.description: A packed package file, or a source directory; - is refused, since a package is read with random access.

operands.name: <path>
operands.description: The entry to read.

flags.name: --lines
flags.description: Print only the lines N, N-M or N- of a text entry.

flags.name: --number
flags.description: Prefix each line printed with its line number and a tab.

flags.name: --limit
flags.description: Lower one resource limit for this run, to a whole number no higher than its default (a size may end in KiB, MiB or GiB). metais limits lists them.

flags.name: --fail-on
flags.description: With warning, a warning fails the command with exit status 1 as an error does; no finding's severity changes.

flags.name: --json
flags.description: Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.

flags.name: --color
flags.description: Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR.

flags.name: --help
flags.description: Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

commands.prints: The entry's bytes, or the lines selected, unchanged; never coloured.

commands.name: outline
commands.description: List the headings of a Markdown entry, each with the lines of its section.
commands.detail:
Reads a text entry as CommonMark 0.31.2 and lists its ATX and setext headings, levels 1 to 6, in document order. A leading frontmatter block is skipped, and its lines still count. What CommonMark does not make a heading, such as a # line in a code block, is not listed.

Each heading is shown with its first line and the last line of its section: the line before the next heading of the same or a higher level, or the entry's last line. So metais read <package> <path> --lines <line>-<end> reads exactly one section. An entry with no headings gives an empty list.

operands.name: <package>
operands.description: A packed package file, or a source directory; - is refused, since a package is read with random access.

operands.name: <path>
operands.description: The text entry to outline.

flags.name: --limit
flags.description: Lower one resource limit for this run, to a whole number no higher than its default (a size may end in KiB, MiB or GiB). metais limits lists them.

flags.name: --fail-on
flags.description: With warning, a warning fails the command with exit status 1 as an error does; no finding's severity changes.

flags.name: --json
flags.description: Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.

flags.name: --color
flags.description: Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR.

flags.name: --help
flags.description: Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

commands.prints: One line per heading: its line and its section's last line, a tab, two spaces per level below 1, the heading's #s and its text.

commands.name: grep
commands.description: Search a package's entries for a regular expression, with context.
commands.detail:
The pattern is RE2 syntax, as Go's regexp defines it, and is matched against each line without its line ending, so ^ and $ anchor the line; a CR before the LF is part of the ending. --ignore-case prepends (?i). The pattern is bounded by the pattern-length, regex-program and regex-work limits.

Globs select the entries searched (metais help globs); with none, every entry is searched but those beneath a segment that begins with a dot, so .compiled/ is searched only when a glob names it. Entries are searched in path order, lines in order. Binary entries are skipped and listed.

--max-results bounds the matching lines reported, from 1 to the grep-matches limit; the search still runs to the end, and counts every matching line. A line longer than 1024 bytes is shown cut, and read --lines gives it whole. No match is not a failure: grep exits 0.

operands.name: <package>
operands.description: A packed package file, or a source directory; - is refused, since a package is read with random access.

operands.name: <pattern>
operands.description: A regular expression in RE2 syntax; write -- before one that begins with -.

operands.name: <glob>
operands.description: A glob selecting the entries to search; every entry when none is given.

flags.name: --context
flags.description: Show n lines before and after each matching line, from 0 to the grep-context limit.

flags.name: --ignore-case
flags.description: Match letters regardless of case.

flags.name: --max-results
flags.description: Report at most n matching lines, from 1 to the grep-matches limit.

flags.name: --limit
flags.description: Lower one resource limit for this run, to a whole number no higher than its default (a size may end in KiB, MiB or GiB). metais limits lists them.

flags.name: --fail-on
flags.description: With warning, a warning fails the command with exit status 1 as an error does; no finding's severity changes.

flags.name: --json
flags.description: Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.

flags.name: --color
flags.description: Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR.

flags.name: --help
flags.description: Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

commands.prints: Each matching line as path:line:text and each line of context as path-line-text, with -- between groups that are not adjacent; a truncation notice and the binary entries skipped go to standard error.

commands.name: schema
commands.description: Print the package's combined input schema, or one input's schema.
commands.detail:
With no input, prints the combined input schema: one JSON Schema 2020-12 document with a property per input, which is what the inputs are validated against. With an input, prints that input's schema as one self-contained document: the input's title and description beside a $ref to its schema, with $defs embedding every schema resource the $ref reaches. A collection's schema is the array's, whose items each file must satisfy.

The schema is printed in canonical key order, indented by two spaces, so metais schema <package> <input> > <input>.json writes a usable schema file.

commands.name: extract
commands.description: Write the entries the globs select to a new directory.
commands.detail:
Writes every entry any glob selects to <dir>/<entry path>, as stored (metais help globs). Every glob must select at least one entry, or nothing is written: a glob that selects nothing is a typo to hear about.

<dir> must not exist: it is created, with its missing parents, and every file is created beneath it, never through a link. An existing <dir> is refused, empty or not, and nothing in it is touched. A failed write stops extract, which lists the files it wrote and removes none of them. --dry-run lists the files it would write, and writes nothing.

commands.name: validate
commands.description: Validate inputs against a package, and report every finding at once.
commands.detail:
Opens and verifies the package as inspect does, then assembles the inputs object: each file of the data directory, then each --inputs-json in command-line order, then each --set and --set-json in command-line order, each replacing what came before at its place. Each schema default is applied to a member left absent, and the whole is validated against the package's schemas and its input constraints.

Every finding is reported in one run: a file that does not parse does not stop the others from being read and validated. With no supply flag, nothing is supplied, and every required input is reported missing.

The result lists, for every input, whether it was supplied and where its value came from. --resolved adds the inputs as templates would see them, after coercion and defaults, in canonical key order; in human form it is printed as indented JSON after the findings.

operands.name: <package>
operands.description: A packed package file, or a source directory; - is refused, since a package is read with random access.

flags.name: --data
flags.description: The data directory: one file per input named <input>.<ext>, and one directory per collection input. metais inspect lists each input's file names.

flags.name: --set
flags.description: Set one value at an inputs pointer, such as /vendor/name=Acme; the text is coerced to the type the schema declares there. Applied after --data and --inputs-json, in command-line order with --set-json.

flags.name: --set-json
flags.description: Set one value at an inputs pointer as JSON text, the way to set null, an array or an object. Applied in command-line order with --set.

flags.name: --inputs-json
flags.description: A JSON object whose members are inputs, each replacing that input's whole value; - reads it from standard input, once. Applied after --data, in command-line order.

flags.name: --resolved
flags.description: Add the inputs as templates would see them: parsed and coerced, with defaults applied, absent members absent.

flags.name: --limit
flags.description: Lower one resource limit for this run, to a whole number no higher than its default (a size may end in KiB, MiB or GiB). metais limits lists them.

flags.name: --fail-on
flags.description: With warning, a warning fails the command with exit status 1 as an error does; no finding's severity changes.

flags.name: --json
flags.description: Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.

flags.name: --color
flags.description: Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR.

flags.name: --help
flags.description: Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

commands.prints: Every finding, then the summary line; with --resolved, the inputs as indented JSON.

commands.name: render
commands.description: Render the package's outputs from the inputs supplied, into a new directory or to standard output.
commands.detail:
The package is opened and verified whole, and the inputs are supplied and validated, as metais inspect and metais validate do; an input that fails ends the render with every finding of the inputs. Then every output is planned, an asset or a mirror as each file it writes, its path checked by the portable-path rules, and rendered in memory: every output is attempted, and each reports its first error. An asset is copied as it is, never rendered: its size counts against the output limits, and its bytes are read from the package as it is written. An output declaring newline: crlf then has its line endings made CR LF, and one naming a validate schema is parsed and validated against it, every finding of every output reported. If any finding is an error, nothing is written anywhere. A container output is one zip of its entries, each rendered as an output is, in the order its profile and its first entries give; its zip is written as it is assembled.

--out is required, and names a directory that does not exist yet. The outputs are written beneath a staging directory beside it, .metais-staging- followed by 16 hex digits, which is then renamed to it in one step that never replaces anything: the directory either does not exist or holds every output. Its missing parents are created. An --out that exists is refused before anything is written.

--out - writes every file to standard output as one pax archive instead, in path order, each entry with mode 0644, or 0755 for an executable output, owner 0 and the time 1980-01-01T00:00:00Z; with --json the document then goes to standard error, after the archive. Standard output carries the archive and nothing else, and nothing at all when the render is refused. An archive is not written to a terminal.

--only <path> selects one file by the path --dry-run lists. The whole render still runs and is checked, so --only never makes a refused render succeed; it chooses what is written: with --out -, the file's bytes alone, which may go to a terminal, and with --out <dir>, that file alone.

--dry-run renders everything and checks --out as a render would, writes nothing anywhere, and lists every file the render would write with its size and digest. It is refused exactly when the render would be.

A template sees the inputs as inputs, the package's identity as package, where each input came from as sources, the output being rendered as output, and the render time as now, which is --now normalized to UTC, or nil without it. Nothing of the host — no environment variable, directory, user or clock — reaches a template.

Each output's path is a Liquid template too. An output with for_each is rendered once for each element of its array, which its when, its path and its template see as item, with its position as fan_out; an output, or an element, whose when is false writes no file.

operands.name: <package>
operands.description: A packed package file, or a source directory; - is refused, since a package is read with random access.

flags.name: --out
flags.description: The directory to render into, which must not exist, or - for an archive on standard output; required.

flags.name: --data
flags.description: The data directory: one file per input named <input>.<ext>, and one directory per collection input. metais inspect lists each input's file names.

flags.name: --set
flags.description: Set one value at an inputs pointer, such as /vendor/name=Acme; the text is coerced to the type the schema declares there. Applied after --data and --inputs-json, in command-line order with --set-json.

flags.name: --set-json
flags.description: Set one value at an inputs pointer as JSON text, the way to set null, an array or an object. Applied in command-line order with --set.

flags.name: --inputs-json
flags.description: A JSON object whose members are inputs, each replacing that input's whole value; - reads it from standard input, once. Applied after --data, in command-line order.

flags.name: --only
flags.description: Write only the file at this path, as --dry-run lists it: its bytes alone with --out -.

flags.name: --dry-run
flags.description: List every file the render would write, with its size and digest, and write nothing.

flags.name: --now
flags.description: The render time, an RFC 3339 date-time with an offset, which templates see as now; without it there is no time.

flags.name: --limit
flags.description: Lower one resource limit for this run, to a whole number no higher than its default (a size may end in KiB, MiB or GiB). metais limits lists them.

flags.name: --fail-on
flags.description: With warning, a warning fails the command with exit status 1 as an error does; no finding's severity changes.

flags.name: --json
flags.description: Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.

flags.name: --color
flags.description: Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR.

flags.name: --help
flags.description: Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

commands.prints: One line per file written, in path order: its size, its digest and its path, separated by tabs; a container's entries are indented beneath it, in its order. On a dry run the lines are headed would write. With --out -, standard output is the archive, or the one file's bytes.

commands.name: init
commands.description: Write a new package's source directory, with an input, a template and an example.
commands.detail:
Writes eight files into <dir>: metais.yaml, one input with its schema and meaning document, one template, one example with its inputs and expected output, and a .gitattributes that keeps git from converting line endings. The scaffold is a small package to edit rather than an empty one.

The package's name is --name, or else the last element of <dir> as written. When <dir> is omitted or ends in . or .., --name is required: metais never looks up the working directory's name. The name must satisfy the package name rule.

<dir> is created, with its missing parents, when it does not exist. An existing <dir> must be empty, apart from names beginning with . (such as .git) other than .compiled and .gitattributes, and files ending .metais; init never overwrites, and refuses anything else, listing up to ten of the entries it found. A failed write stops init, which lists the files it wrote and removes none of them.

commands.name: check
commands.description: Check a package without data, and report every finding of every step at once.
commands.detail:
The package is a source directory, the current directory when omitted, or a packed package file. check reads nothing but the package and writes nothing. It runs every step in order: the source tree, the entries, the limits of the package pack would write, the manifest and its guide's links, every schema with its defaults, examples, consts, enums and required names, every template, the cross-reference of templates against schemas, Office Open XML text runs, the examples' layout, and the compiled form. Each step runs whatever an earlier one found; a step whose input could not be made is named in one report.step_skipped finding.

A package that cannot be read at all — its container, its entry names, its digests or its source tree — is refused with the findings every command gives it.

check exits 1 when any finding is an error; warnings do not fail it unless --fail-on warning is given.

commands.name: unpack
commands.description: Write a packed package's source directory, to edit it.
commands.detail:
Writes every entry of the packed package into <dir>, as the source directory it was packed from: the manifest as its author wrote it, the inputs, templates, references, assets and examples. .compiled/ is not written: it is derived from the rest, and metais pack writes it again. Files are written with mode 0644 and directories 0755, less the umask, whatever the package records.

Before it writes anything, unpack verifies the whole package as inspect does, its digests included, and refuses a package that fails, writing nothing. It does not run check: a package with check errors is the one an author needs to unpack and fix. A source directory is refused: it is already what unpack would write.

--to is required. A <dir> that does not exist is created, with its missing parents, by writing beside it and renaming the whole directory into place, so a failed write leaves nothing. An existing <dir> must be empty, apart from names beginning with . (such as .git) other than .compiled, and files ending .metais; it is written in place, and a failed write stops unpack, which lists the files it wrote and removes none of them. There is no --overwrite: a file left from an earlier tree would join the unpacked source and be packed with it.

operands.name: <package>
operands.description: A packed package file; - is refused, since a package is read with random access.

flags.name: --to
flags.description: The directory to write the source directory into: one that does not exist yet, or an empty one.

flags.name: --limit
flags.description: Lower one resource limit for this run, to a whole number no higher than its default (a size may end in KiB, MiB or GiB). metais limits lists them.

flags.name: --fail-on
flags.description: With warning, a warning fails the command with exit status 1 as an error does; no finding's severity changes.

flags.name: --json
flags.description: Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.

flags.name: --color
flags.description: Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR.

flags.name: --help
flags.description: Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

commands.prints: The files written, relative to <dir>, in the order written.

metais --version, before any command, is this command.

Every size, count and ratio metais reads, computes or writes is bounded, and every bound has a name and a default. A package within every package limit is portable: every conforming tool accepts it at the defaults. A limit may be lowered for one run, and is never raised.

topics.name: inputs
topics.title: Supplying a package's inputs, and which source wins.
topics.text:
A package declares its inputs, each with a schema, and a caller supplies them
from three sources, applied in this order, each to the result of the one before:

1. The data directory, given with --data: one file per input, named after the
   input with the extension of its form (vendor.json, criteria.csv), or one
   directory per collection input. Each gives its input's whole value. A file
   that names no declared input is a finding, and so is a second file for one
   input.
2. Each --inputs-json, in command-line order: a JSON object whose members are
   input names, each replacing that input's whole value; values are never
   merged. --inputs-json - reads the object from standard input, once.
3. Each path set, in command-line order: --set /input/pointer=text sets one
   value at a JSON Pointer whose first token is an input's name, coercing the
   text by the schema; --set-json /input/pointer=json sets it to a JSON value,
   which is how null, an array or an object is set. Each replaces only the value
   at its pointer.

The order is fixed by kind, not by position: every --inputs-json applies before
every path set, wherever they are written, and among one kind the later wins. To
change one nested value and keep the rest, use a path set; --inputs-json
replaces the whole input.

Defaults from the schemas are applied after all three, and then the inputs are
validated, every finding at once.

topics.name: globs
topics.title: The patterns that select a package's entries.
topics.text:
A glob selects a package's entries by path. It is matched against the whole
entry path, segment by segment, with / as the separator, and is case-sensitive.

  *       matches any run of characters within one segment.
  ?       matches one character other than /.
  [...]   matches one character in a class; lo-hi is a range.
  [^...]  matches one character not in a class.
  \       makes the next character literal.
  **      standing alone as a segment, matches zero or more whole segments; **
          anywhere else is a usage error.

There are no braces. *, ?, [...] and ** never match a segment that begins with a
dot; a pattern segment that itself begins with a dot matches one. So **/*.md
does not reach into .compiled/, and .compiled/** does. A pattern with no
wildcard that names a directory selects every entry beneath it.

topics.name: json
topics.title: The JSON document every command prints with --json.
topics.text:
With --json, a run prints exactly one JSON document on standard output: compact
UTF-8 with no byte order mark, one line ending in one LF, HTML escaping off, and
standard error empty. Its members are always present, in this order:

  format    The document's name and major version, metais.<command>/<major>.
  ok        True when the command completed and no finding is an error.
  findings  The findings, in the specification's order; [] when there are none.
            A usage error is a finding too.
  summary   The exact counts of errors, warnings and info, how many findings are
            listed and omitted, and the count of each code.
  result    The command's result, or null when it was refused before producing
            one.
  next      The commands to run next, each {"run", "why"}; [] when there is
            nothing to suggest, and never empty after a refusal.

The exit status is the same with and without --json, and --json is honoured even
on a command line that does not parse. Within a major version a format only
gains members and enumeration values: ignore a member you do not know, and read
an unknown value as other.

The formats:
  metais.inspect/1   metais inspect
  metais.ls/1        metais ls
  metais.read/1      metais read
  metais.outline/1   metais outline
  metais.grep/1      metais grep
  metais.schema/1    metais schema
  metais.extract/1   metais extract
  metais.validate/1  metais validate
  metais.render/1    metais render
  metais.init/1      metais init
  metais.check/1     metais check
  metais.unpack/1    metais unpack
  metais.version/1   metais version
  metais.limits/1    metais limits
  metais.help/1      metais help
  metais.usage/1     a line that names no command

topics.name: exit-codes
topics.title: What each exit status means.
topics.text:
metais exits with the same status with and without --json:

  0  Success, warnings included; help, version and limits.
  1  An error in content: invalid inputs, a failing check or test, an output
     refused by its schema or its path, a package's own defect under an
     authoring command, or a warning under --fail-on warning.
  2  A defect in metais itself (internal.error), or the Go runtime's status
     after a crash.
  3  The command line is wrong: an unknown command or flag, a missing or extra
     operand, a malformed or repeated flag, or no command at all.
  4  The package is refused: not found, unreadable, out of specification, a
     digest mismatch, an unsupported specification version or a package limit;
     or a package's own defect under a consuming command.
  5  The destination is refused: not empty without --overwrite, a link or
     special file in the way, or a failed write.

When several apply, the first in the order 2, 3, 4, 1, 5 is the status: fixing a
destination alone would not help a run whose inputs are invalid.

The command line is wrong: an unknown command or flag, a missing or extra operand, a malformed or repeated flag, or no command at all.
